label: pass
title: Bulk import books from CSV
body:
Support bulk catalogue updates:

1. New `src/csv.js` exporting `parseCsv(text)` → array of rows (arrays of strings), RFC 4180: quoted fields, `""` escapes, commas and newlines inside quotes, CRLF or LF line endings, optional trailing newline (no empty trailing row).
2. `POST /books/import` — the request body is the raw CSV **string** (the handler receives it as `req.body`). Header row must contain `id,title,author,price,stock,tags` (any order; extra columns ignored) → otherwise `400 { error }`.
   - `price` is dollars (e.g. `39.99`) → store `priceCents` (rounded); `tags` are `;`-separated (empty → `[]`); `stock` must be a non-negative integer; `id` and `title` are required; price must be a number ≥ 0.
   - Existing ids are updated (title, author, price, tags, and stock set to the given value); new ids are created.
   - Invalid rows are skipped and reported. Response `200 { created, updated, errors: [{ line, message }] }` where `line` is the 1-based line of the CSV text where that record **starts** (quoted fields can span lines).
3. Add tests.
plan:
Add CSV parser and /books/import endpoint to support bulk CSV import with validations, update inventory accordingly, and add tests.
1. Add CSV parser implementation
2. Add /books/import route handler in src/server.js
3. Add tests for CSV import in test/server.test.js
requirements: Add new file src/csv.js exporting parseCsv(text) that implements RFC 4180: quoted fields with "" escapes, commas/newlines inside quotes, handles CRLF or LF line endings, optional trailing newline (no empty trailing row), and returns an array of rows (each row is an array of strings).

Add POST /books/import route in src/server.js that accepts raw CSV string in req.body, validates header row contains columns id,title,author,price,stock,tags (case-insensitive, trimmed; order may vary; extra columns ignored) and returns 400 { error } if missing required columns.

CSV handler must parse rows, validate fields per-row: id and title required; price is dollars string/number >= 0 and converted to priceCents using Math.round(dollars * 100); stock must be non-negative integer; tags split by ';' into array (empty -> []); invalid rows are skipped and collected with their starting line number (1-based) and a message.
Existing inventory entries (by id) are updated: set title, author, priceCents, tags, and stock to given values; new ids are created.
If duplicate ids occur in file, process in file order so later rows override earlier ones.

Response 200 { created, updated, errors: [{ line, message }] } where created and updated are counts and errors list contains the appropriate line where the CSV record starts (quoted fields can span lines).
Add tests in test/server.test.js that exercise successful import creating and updating books and reporting errors for invalid rows and missing headers.
summary:
Added CSV parser (src/csv.js) with parseCsv and parseCsvWithLines implementing RFC4180-like behavior and line tracking. Added POST /books/import route in src/server.js that accepts raw CSV text from req.body, validates headers (case-insensitive trimmed), parses rows, validates fields (id, title, price >=0 -> priceCents via Math.round, non-negative integer stock, tags split by ';'), updates existing inventory entries or creates new ones, skips invalid rows and reports errors with 1-based starting line numbers. Added tests in test/server.test.js for successful import, error reporting, and missing headers. Verified by running npm test — all new tests pass; one pre-existing failing test (math.divide) remains unchanged.

diff --git a/src/csv.js b/src/csv.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..5bd1ce5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/csv.js
@@ -0,0 +1,124 @@
+// Minimal RFC 4180 CSV parser
+// Exports parseCsv(text) -> array of rows (arrays of strings)
+// Also exports parseCsvWithLines(text) -> array of { row: string[], startLine: number }
+export function parseCsv(text) {
+  return parseCsvWithLines(text).map(r => r.row)
+}
+
+export function parseCsvWithLines(text) {
+  if (text == null) return []
+  const rows = []
+  let i = 0
+  const len = text.length
+  let cur = ''
+  let row = []
+  let inQuotes = false
+  let line = 1
+  let rowStartLine = 1
+
+  const pushField = () => {
+    row.push(cur)
+    cur = ''
+  }
+  const pushRow = () => {
+    // avoid adding an empty trailing row when text ends with newline
+    // but we still add rows that have at least one field or were started
+    rows.push({ row: row.slice(), startLine: rowStartLine })
+    row = []
+  }
+
+  while (i < len) {
+    const ch = text[i]
+    if (inQuotes) {
+      if (ch === '"') {
+        // peek next
+        if (i + 1 < len && text[i + 1] === '"') {
+          cur += '"'
+          i += 2
+          continue
+        } else {
+          inQuotes = false
+          i++
+          continue
+        }
+      } else {
+        if (ch === '\r') {
+          // handle CRLF or lone CR
+          if (i + 1 < len && text[i + 1] === '\n') {
+            cur += '\n'
+            i += 2
+            line++
+            continue
+          } else {
+            cur += '\n'
+            i++
+            line++
+            continue
+          }
+        }
+        if (ch === '\n') {
+          cur += '\n'
+          i++
+          line++
+          continue
+        }
+        cur += ch
+        i++
+        continue
+      }
+    } else {
+      if (ch === ',') {
+        pushField()
+        i++
+        continue
+      }
+      if (ch === '"') {
+        inQuotes = true
+        i++
+        continue
+      }
+      if (ch === '\r') {
+        pushField()
+        // end row
+        if (i + 1 < len && text[i + 1] === '\n') i++
+        pushRow()
+        i++
+        line++
+        rowStartLine = line
+        continue
+      }
+      if (ch === '\n') {
+        pushField()
+        pushRow()
+        i++
+        line++
+        rowStartLine = line
+        continue
+      }
+      cur += ch
+      i++
+      continue
+    }
+  }
+
+  // end of input
+  if (inQuotes) {
+    // unterminated quote: treat as field end
+    // (best-effort)
+  }
+  // if there's remaining data or the last char ended a field
+  if (cur !== '' || row.length > 0) {
+    pushField()
+    pushRow()
+  }
+
+  // Remove a trailing empty row if the text ends with a newline and produced an empty last row
+  if (rows.length > 0) {
+    const last = rows[rows.length - 1]
+    if (last.row.length === 1 && last.row[0] === '' && (text.endsWith('\n') || text.endsWith('\r'))) {
+      rows.pop()
+    }
+  }
+
+  return rows
+}
diff --git a/src/server.js b/src/server.js
index 0969320..d6446d0 100644
--- a/src/server.js
+++ b/src/server.js
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
 import http from 'node:http'
 import { Router } from './router.js'
 import { Inventory } from './inventory.js'
+import { parseCsvWithLines } from './csv.js'
 import { Cart } from './cart.js'
 import { formatCurrency } from './format.js'
 
@@ -29,6 +30,62 @@ export function createApp(inventory = Inventory.fromFile()) {
     return { status: 200, body: { totalCents: total, total: formatCurrency(total) } }
   })
 
+  router.post('/books/import', ({ body }) => {
+    // body is raw CSV text
+    if (typeof body !== 'string') return { status: 400, body: { error: 'Request body must be raw CSV text' } }
+    const rowsWithLines = parseCsvWithLines(body)
+    if (rowsWithLines.length === 0) return { status: 200, body: { created: 0, updated: 0, errors: [] } }
+    const header = rowsWithLines[0].row.map(h => String(h).trim().toLowerCase())
+    const required = ['id', 'title', 'author', 'price', 'stock', 'tags']
+    const idx = {}
+    for (let i = 0; i < header.length; i++) idx[header[i]] = i
+    for (const r of required) if (!(r in idx)) return { status: 400, body: { error: `Missing required columns: ${required.join(',')}` } }
+
+    let created = 0, updated = 0
+    const errors = []
+    // process data rows
+    for (let ri = 1; ri < rowsWithLines.length; ri++) {
+      const { row, startLine } = rowsWithLines[ri]
+      const get = (name) => {
+        const i = idx[name]
+        return i != null ? (row[i] ?? '') : ''
+      }
+      const id = String(get('id') ?? '').trim()
+      const title = String(get('title') ?? '').trim()
+      const author = String(get('author') ?? '').trim()
+      const priceRaw = String(get('price') ?? '').trim()
+      const stockRaw = String(get('stock') ?? '').trim()
+      const tagsRaw = String(get('tags') ?? '')
+
+      if (!id) { errors.push({ line: startLine, message: 'id is required' }); continue }
+      if (!title) { errors.push({ line: startLine, message: 'title is required' }); continue }
+
+      const priceNum = Number(priceRaw)
+      if (!Number.isFinite(priceNum) || priceNum < 0) { errors.push({ line: startLine, message: 'price must be a number >= 0' }); continue }
+      const priceCents = Math.round(priceNum * 100)
+
+      if (!/^-?\d+$/.test(stockRaw) || Number(stockRaw) < 0) { errors.push({ line: startLine, message: 'stock must be a non-negative integer' }); continue }
+      const stock = Number(stockRaw)
+
+      const tags = tagsRaw === '' ? [] : tagsRaw.split(';').map(s => s.trim()).filter(s => s)
+
+      const existing = inventory.find(id)
+      if (existing) {
+        existing.title = title
+        existing.author = author
+        existing.priceCents = priceCents
+        existing.tags = tags
+        existing.stock = stock
+        updated++
+      } else {
+        inventory.books.set(id, { id, title, author, priceCents, tags, stock })
+        created++
+      }
+    }
+
+    return { status: 200, body: { created, updated, errors } }
+  })
+
   return async function handle(req) {
     const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
     const match = router.match(req.method, url.pathname)

+
+  const res = await handle({ method: 'POST', url: '/books/import', body: csv })

+  assert.equal(res.body.errors.length, 3)
+
+  // verify inventory was updated/created
+  const nb = inventory.find('nb1')
+  assert.equal(nb.title, 'New Book')
+  const b2 = inventory.find('b2')
+  assert.equal(b2.stock, 10)
+})
+
+test('POST /books/import missing required headers returns 400', async () => {
+  const inventory = Inventory.fromFile()
+  const handle = createApp(inventory)
+  const csv = `id,name,price\n1,One,9.99\n`
+  const res = await handle({ method: 'POST', url: '/books/import', body: csv })
+  assert.equal(res.status, 400)
+  assert.ok(res.body.error)
+})
